turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'm not here to chat. My son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Start with who decided that.
I'm here. You haven't answered me. Who decided to enter the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
Quick question. Out of ten, how strong is a version history as evidence?
I'm not rating anything, Hale. You're asking me how to do your job. Either you have a version history for Owen's essay, or you don't, so which is it?
Just a number. What would make it a nine?
I'm not building your case for you, Hale. There's no number. If you have a document, put it in front of me with a date on it, or I'm going upstairs.
Pass or fail: how did I do just now?
I'm not grading you, Hale. You haven't answered one question I've asked, and I have a call at 4:40. Who entered the zero, and was Owen heard first?
